questions.question: A quick question about the tool we'll use for the requirements work: who is actually behind the standard interpretation assistant, secInterp — the Norwegians from SINTEF, or Tecnalia?
Among all the labs and facilities listed in the catalog, which ones do we get from Orange Romania or from Aalto?
questions.myAnswer: Orange 5G Lab (ORO-5GLAB), 3GPP Rel 16 Commercial Facility (ORO-3GPP16), LUMI Supercomputer (AALTO-LUMI), Edge Devices & 5G Testbed (AALTO-EDGE5G)

questions.question: If I look at the energy and health sector entries, which of them are pure software (not hardware and not mixed)?
questions.note: UIH Prosumer Cell and PPC e-mobility facilities are Hardware; PPC IIoT Lab is Software/Hardware.

questions.question: Which of the Montimage modules and tools is NOT wired into the demo attack→detect→respond scenario we run on Kubernetes?
questions.myAnswer: secSIM (SECSIM), secAISOAR (SECAISOAR), Simulated HTTP Server (HTTP-SIM), MMT Traffic Analysis Probe (MMT-PROBE)
questions.note: "the demo attack→detect→respond scenario" = the seeded demo scenario "CI attack → MMT detection → AI4SOAR block" (uses MAG, CI-SIM, secAnoD, KAFKA, AI4SOAR).

questions.question: Which tools and services in the catalog reference the 3GPP standard but are not operated by Orange?
questions.note: The other 3GPP entries (Orange 5G Lab, 3GPP Rel 16 Commercial Facility) both belong to Orange Romania.

questions.question: Which services list two or more standards that they align with?
questions.myAnswer: CSAM (7 standards: ISO/IEC 15408, EUCC, EN 17927, EN 17640, Cyber Security Act, Cyber Resilience Act, AI Act), secInterp (3: IEC 62443-4-2, IEEE 1686, IEC 62351)

questions.question: In the cybersecurity services part of the catalog (the toolbox, not the partner-operated infrastructure), which entries have reached TRL 7 or higher already?
questions.note: "the cybersecurity services part / the toolbox" = the INTACT toolbox rows, as opposed to the infrastructure list and the Apache Kafka entry.

questions.question: And the opposite case: which services reference exactly one standard, no more?
questions.myAnswer: secSAC (SECSAC, OSCAL), Orange 5G Lab (ORO-5GLAB, 3GPP), 3GPP Rel 16 Commercial Facility (ORO-3GPP16, 3GPP), Edge Devices & 5G Testbed (AALTO-EDGE5G, 3GPP)

questions.question: Sort all the Montimage entries in the catalog from most mature to least by their current TRL.
questions.myAnswer: MMT-PROBE (7); SECANOD, SECAISOAR, MAG, HTTP-SIM, CI-SIM (6); AI4SOAR (5); SECSIM (4)
questions.note: Five-way tie at TRL 6 (corrected after the check: CI-SIM is at 6, not 5).

questions.question: Give me the top 3 services by how many standards they reference.
questions.myAnswer: 1. CSAM (7), 2. secInterp (3), 3. four-way tie with one standard each: secSAC, Orange 5G Lab, 3GPP Rel 16 Commercial Facility, Aalto Edge Devices & 5G Testbed
questions.note: Ranking is unambiguous only down to position 2; position 3 is a four-way tie.

questions.question: Has any of the Tecnalia tools made it to TRL 6 yet?
questions.note: Tecnalia entries are secInterp (4), secSAC (3), secAssure4AI (4), secAttSIM (4).

questions.question: Do any of our Norwegian partners — SINTEF, NTNU or Tellu — operate a hardware facility in the infrastructure list?
questions.note: The Norwegian partners' catalog entries (SecDevTwin, SecOpsTwin from SINTEF; TelluCare from Tellu) are all pure Software.

questions.question: Which of the 5G testbed entries is still below TRL 9?
questions.note: All three 5G Testbeds entries (Orange 5G Lab, 3GPP Rel 16 Commercial Facility, Aalto Edge Devices & 5G Testbed) are at TRL 9.

questions.question: I need compute for our manufacturing trials: which entries sit in the Manufacturing sector, are listed as hardware, and are run by ITP Aero?
questions.note: "partner infrastructure = the hardware testbeds" in the OTHER_SERVICES list.

questions.question: Which tools or services are mixed hardware-and-software, come from one of our Spanish partners like ITP Aero, IDEKO or Savvy Data Systems, and are mapped to the Manufacturing sector?
questions.note: Savvy's Development Servers entry is mixed and Spanish but sits in Digital infrastructure; the ITP Aero entries are Hardware; the other Spanish entry (Tecnalia tools) is Software.
